title: ISO
description: Sensor sensitivity management for clean images and controlled noise.
summary: ISO sets the camera's sensitivity to light; professionals use it to finish exposure after aperture and shutter priorities while staying inside clean native ranges.

knowledgeItem.title: ISO
knowledgeItem.description: Sensor sensitivity management for clean images and controlled noise.
definitions: ISO sets the camera's sensitivity to light; professionals use it to finish exposure after aperture and shutter priorities while staying inside clean native ranges.
rules: If noise threatens product texture, add light before raising ISO.
Always note ISO on camera reports for continuity.
When dual-native exists, jump intentionally—do not linger in noisy midpoints.
Never 'fix exposure with ISO' as a substitute for lighting design.
bestPractices: Prefer native/base ISO ranges for hero imagery.
Raise ISO only after aperture and lighting options are exhausted (or intentionally).
Keep ISO consistent across a scene when possible.
Evaluate noise on the actual delivery size, not only the monitor.
